1→# Discord Adapter Design Spec
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-03-23
     4→**Status:** Approved
     5→
     6→## Overview
     7→
     8→Add a built-in Discord adapter to OpenACP with full feature parity with the Telegram adapter. Uses discord.js library and maps Telegram concepts (forum topics, inline keyboards, callback queries) to Discord equivalents (forum channel posts, button components, interactions).
     9→
    10→## Architecture: Mirror Approach
    11→
    12→Replicate the Telegram adapter's file structure 1:1 in `src/adapters/discord/`, mapping each Telegram concept to its Discord equivalent. No shared base class extraction — keep adapters independent.
    13→
    14→## File Structure
    15→
    16→```
    17→src/adapters/discord/
    18→  adapter.ts              — Main DiscordAdapter class
    19→  index.ts                — Re-exports
    20→  types.ts                — DiscordChannelConfig, DiscordPlatformData
    21→  forums.ts               — Forum post/thread CRUD + auto-unarchive helper
    22→  streaming.ts            — MessageDraft (2000 char limit)
    23→  send-queue.ts           — DiscordSendQueue with rate limiting
    24→  permissions.ts          — Button-based permission handler
    25→  formatting.ts           — Markdown formatting for Discord
    26→  activity.ts             — ThinkingIndicator, UsageMessage, PlanCard, ActivityTracker
    27→  tool-call-tracker.ts    — Tool call state tracking
    28→  draft-manager.ts        — DraftManager for streaming
    29→  skill-command-manager.ts — Skill command pinning via thread.messages.pin()
    30→  action-detect.ts        — Action detection + button building
    31→  assistant.ts            — Assistant session (channelId: "discord") in dedicated thread
    32→  commands/
    33→    index.ts              — Slash command registration (guild.commands.set() full replace)
    34→    menu.ts               — Menu interactions
    35→    new-session.ts        — /new command flow
    36→    session.ts            — /cancel, /status, /sessions, /handoff
    37→    admin.ts              — /dangerous, /restart, /update
    38→    agents.ts             — /agents, /install
    39→    integrate.ts          — /integrate
    40→    settings.ts           — /settings
    41→    doctor.ts             — /doctor
    42→
    43→src/core/doctor/checks/
    44→  discord.ts              — Discord-specific doctor check (token, guild, forum channel)
    45→```
    46→
    47→## Config
    48→
    49→Added to `config.channels`:
    50→
    51→```json
    52→{
    53→  "channels": {
    54→    "discord": {
    55→      "enabled": false,
    56→      "botToken": "YOUR_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN",
    57→      "guildId": "",
    58→      "forumChannelId": null,
    59→      "notificationChannelId": null,
    60→      "assistantThreadId": null
    61→    }
    62→  }
    63→}
    64→```
    65→
    66→All fields use `.default()` or `.optional()` for backward compatibility.
    67→
    68→**Type:**
    69→
    70→```ts
    71→interface DiscordChannelConfig {
    72→  enabled: boolean
    73→  botToken: string
    74→  guildId: string
    75→  forumChannelId: string | null
    76→  notificationChannelId: string | null
    77→  assistantThreadId: string | null
    78→}
    79→```
    80→
    81→**Platform data** (defined in `src/core/types.ts` alongside `TelegramPlatformData`):
    82→
    83→```ts
    84→interface DiscordPlatformData {
    85→  threadId: string
    86→  skillMsgId?: string
    87→}
    88→```
    89→
    90→**Env overrides** (fallback for Docker/CI, not primary flow — must be wired into `applyEnvOverrides()` in `config.ts`):
    91→- `OPENACP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` → `channels.discord.botToken`
    92→- `OPENACP_DISCORD_GUILD_ID` → `channels.discord.guildId`
    93→
    94→**Primary flow:** Token entered via interactive setup → saved to `config.json`.
    95→
    96→## Platform Mapping
    97→
    98→| Concern | Telegram | Discord |
    99→|---|---|---|
   100→| Message limit | 4096 chars | 2000 chars |
   101→| Streaming | `editMessageText` | `message.edit()` |
   102→| Buttons | InlineKeyboard + callback queries | ActionRow + ButtonBuilder + interactions |
   103→| Interaction timeout | No timeout | 3s acknowledgment required |
   104→| Thread model | Forum topics (integer `message_thread_id`) | Forum posts (string `threadId`) |
   105→| Commands | `bot.command()` text commands | Slash commands (guild-registered via `guild.commands.set()`) |
   106→| Formatting | HTML (`<b>`, `<code>`) | Native Markdown (`**bold**`, `` `code` ``) |
   107→| Rate limits | ~30 msg/sec per chat | 50 req/sec global, 5 msg/sec per channel |
   108→| Bot setup | BotFather token | Token + Guild ID + Privileged Gateway Intents |
   109→| Typing indicator | `sendChatAction('typing')` | `channel.sendTyping()` |
   110→| Deep links | `https://t.me/c/{id}/{msgId}` | `https://discord.com/channels/{guildId}/{channelId}/{msgId}` |
   111→| Thread archival | N/A | Auto-archive (1h/24h/3d/1w) — must unarchive before sending |
   112→
   113→## Startup Sequence
   114→
   115→`DiscordAdapter.start()`:
   116→
   117→1. Create `Client` with intents: `Guilds`, `GuildMessages`, `MessageContent` (privileged — requires Developer Portal toggle)
   118→2. Instantiate `ToolCallTracker`, `DraftManager`, `SkillCommandManager`
   119→3. `client.login(botToken)`
   120→4. On `ready`:
   121→   - Verify bot is in configured guild (throw if not)
   122→   - `ensureForums()` — create Forum Channel + Notification Channel if `null`, persist IDs to config
   123→   - Register slash commands to guild (`guild.commands.set()` — full replace, propagation delay is expected)
   124→   - Create `PermissionHandler`
   125→   - Set up `interactionCreate` handler (slash commands + button routing)
   126→   - Set up `messageCreate` handler (message routing)
   127→   - Spawn assistant session (`channelId: "discord"`, with Discord-specific system prompt)
   128→   - Set `assistantInitializing = true` during system prompt — suppress adapter output until ready
   129→   - Send welcome message to notification channel
   130→
   131→`DiscordAdapter.stop()`:
   132→
   133→1. Destroy assistant session if active (`this.assistantSession.destroy()`)
   134→2. `client.destroy()` — disconnects from Discord gateway
   135→3. Log "Discord bot stopped"
   136→
   137→## Event Flow
   138→
   139→### Message Routing (`messageCreate`)
   140→
   141→```
   142→User sends message in forum thread
   143→  → guildId check (reject if wrong guild)
   144→  → ignore bot messages (including self)
   145→  → ignore DMs (only process guild messages)
   146→  → threadId = message.channelId
   147→  → core.handleMessage({ channelId: 'discord', threadId, userId, text })
   148→```
   149→
   150→### Interaction Routing (`interactionCreate`)
   151→
   152→```
   153→Button clicked or slash command used
   154→  → interaction.deferReply() or interaction.deferUpdate() (within 3s)
   155→  → Route by type:
   156→    - ChatInputCommand → slash command handlers
   157→    - Button → customId prefix routing (p:, m:, d:, a:, ag:, na:)
   158→```
   159→
   160→### sendMessage() Dispatch
   161→
   162→Suppress output if `assistantInitializing && sessionId === assistantSession.id`.
   163→
   164→| Type | Discord Action |
   165→|---|---|
   166→| `text` | `DraftManager.append()` → `message.edit()` streaming → split at 2000 chars |
   167→| `thought` | `ActivityTracker.onThought()` → `channel.sendTyping()` |
   168→| `tool_call` | `DraftManager.finalize()` → `ToolCallTracker.trackNewCall()` → send embed |
   169→| `tool_update` | `ToolCallTracker.updateCall()` → edit embed on terminal status |
   170→| `plan` | `ActivityTracker.onPlan()` → embed with plan entries |
   171→| `usage` | `DraftManager.finalize()` → usage embed → notification channel (deep link: `https://discord.com/channels/{guildId}/{channelId}/{msgId}`) |
   172→| `session_end` | `DraftManager.finalize()` → cleanup → "Done" message |
   173→| `error` | `DraftManager.finalize()` → error embed |
   174→
   175→### Permission Flow
   176→
   177→```
   178→AgentInstance.onPermissionRequest
   179→  → session.permissionGate.setPending(request)
   180→  → adapter.sendPermissionRequest()
   181→    → Send message with ActionRow buttons (customId: "p:<key>:<optionId>")
   182→  → User clicks button
   183→  → interactionCreate handler matches "p:" prefix
   184→    → interaction.deferUpdate()
   185→    → session.permissionGate.resolve(optionId)
   186→    → Edit message to remove buttons (editReply with empty components)
   187→  → Promise resolves → ACP subprocess continues
   188→```
   189→
   190→Auto-approve: `session.dangerousMode = true` or description contains `"openacp"`.
   191→
   192→### Session Thread Lifecycle
   193→
   194→1. `/new` slash command → `interaction.deferReply()`
   195→2. Create forum post in `forumChannelId` → get thread
   196→3. `core.handleNewSession()` → spawns agent
   197→4. `session.threadId = thread.id`
   198→5. Auto-name event → `thread.setName()`
   199→
   200→### Thread Auto-Archive Handling
   201→
   202→Discord auto-archives inactive threads. The `forums.ts` module provides an `ensureUnarchived(thread)` helper that calls `thread.setArchived(false)` if needed. This helper is called in `sendMessage()` before any message send/edit operation, and in `forums.ts` thread lookup methods.
   203→
   204→### deleteSessionThread()
   205→
   206→Override the base class no-op: call `thread.delete()` to remove the forum post when a session is cleaned up.
   207→
   208→### sendSkillCommands()
   209→
   210→Pin a message containing skill commands in the session thread via `message.pin()`. Persist the `skillMsgId` in `DiscordPlatformData`. On cleanup, unpin and delete the message.
   211→
   212→### /handoff Command
   213→
   214→Same as Telegram: generates a terminal resume command for agents supporting `supportsResume`. Responds as an ephemeral reply in the interaction.
   215→
   216→## Integration Points
   217→
   218→### config.ts
   219→
   220→- Add Discord default config to `channels` with all fields `.default()` or `.optional()`
   221→- Add `OPENACP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and `OPENACP_DISCORD_GUILD_ID` to `applyEnvOverrides()` array
   222→
   223→### setup.ts
   224→
   225→Refactor `runSetup()` to support multiple channels:
   226→
   227→1. Add channel selection step: "Which channels do you want to enable?" → Telegram, Discord, or both
   228→2. If Telegram selected: run existing `setupTelegram()` flow
   229→3. If Discord selected: run `setupDiscord()`:
   230→   - Prompt for Bot Token (with link to Developer Portal)
   231→   - Validate token via `GET /users/@me` API call
   232→   - Prompt for Guild ID (with instructions: Developer Mode → right-click server → Copy ID)
   233→4. Construct `channels` object based on selections (handle telegram-only, discord-only, both cases)
   234→5. Update step counter to be dynamic based on selections (not hardcoded `[1/3]`)
   235→
   236→### main.ts
   237→
   238→Add built-in adapter lookup:
   239→
   240→```ts
   241→} else if (channelName === 'discord') {
   242→  core.registerAdapter('discord', new DiscordAdapter(core, channelConfig as any))
   243→  log.info({ adapter: 'discord' }, 'Adapter registered')
   244→}
   245→```
   246→
   247→Address `TopicManager` Telegram coupling: when Discord is enabled without Telegram, `TopicManager` receives `null` adapter. Either:
   248→- Make `TopicManager` adapter-agnostic (accept any adapter), or
   249→- Skip `TopicManager` creation when Telegram adapter is not present (it's only used by the API server for Telegram topic operations)
   250→
   251→Recommended: skip `TopicManager` when no Telegram adapter, since it's Telegram-specific.
   252→
   253→### package.json
   254→
   255→Add `discord.js` dependency.
   256→
   257→### core/doctor/checks/discord.ts
   258→
   259→Add Discord-specific doctor check:
   260→- Validate bot token format
   261→- Test API reachability (`GET /users/@me`)
   262→- Verify guild membership
   263→- Verify forum channel exists and is accessible
   264→
   265→## Security
   266→
   267→- **Guild restriction:** Only accept messages from configured `guildId`
   268→- **User allowlist:** Uses existing `security.allowedUserIds` from core config
   269→- **Ignore bot messages:** Skip all messages from bots (including self)
   270→- **Ignore DMs:** Only process messages from guild channels
   271→
   272→## Error Handling
   273→
   274→| Scenario | Handling |
   275→|---|---|
   276→| Bot disconnected | discord.js auto-reconnects. Log warning. |
   277→| Guild not found | `start()` throws: "Bot is not in guild {guildId}" |
   278→| Forum channel deleted | Detect on send, recreate + log + update config |
   279→| Rate limited | discord.js built-in rate limit queue. `DiscordSendQueue.onRateLimited()` drops all queued text-type edits (same pattern as Telegram's `TelegramSendQueue`). |
   280→| Message too long | Split at 2000 chars on `\n\n` boundaries, respect code blocks |
   281→| Interaction expired | Already deferred upfront. If followup fails, send new message. |
   282→| Thread archived | `ensureUnarchived(thread)` in `forums.ts` called before sends |
   283→| DM received | Silently ignored (guild-only) |
   284→
   285→## Testing
   286→
   287→Unit tests mock discord.js Client. Test each module independently.
   288→
   289→```
   290→tests/adapters/discord/
   291→  streaming.test.ts
   292→  send-queue.test.ts
   293→  permissions.test.ts
   294→  formatting.test.ts
   295→  tool-call-tracker.test.ts
   296→  adapter.test.ts
   297→```
   298→
   299→## Discord Bot Prerequisites
   300→
   301→1. Create application at discord.com/developers
   302→2. Add bot under "Bot" settings
   303→3. **Enable privileged intent:** Under "Bot" → "Privileged Gateway Intents" → toggle ON "MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT" (required to read message content; without this, `message.content` is empty)
   304→4. Generate invite URL with scopes: `bot`, `applications.commands`
   305→5. Bot permissions: Send Messages, Manage Threads, Create Public Threads, Read Message History, Use Slash Commands, Manage Channels, Embed Links
   306→6. Invite bot to server
   307→7. Enable Developer Mode in Discord (Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode)
   308→8. Right-click your server → "Copy Server ID" → this is your Guild ID
   309→

1→import { Client, GatewayIntentBits, MessageFlags, type Guild, type ForumChannel, type TextChannel, type ThreadChannel } from 'discord.js'
     2→import { ChannelAdapter } from '../../core/channel.js'
     3→import type { OutgoingMessage, PermissionRequest, NotificationMessage, AgentCommand, PlanEntry } from '../../core/types.js'
     4→import type { OpenACPCore } from '../../core/core.js'
     5→import type { Session } from '../../core/session.js'
     6→import { log } from '../../core/log.js'
     7→import type { DiscordChannelConfig } from './types.js'
     8→import { DiscordSendQueue } from './send-queue.js'
     9→import { ToolCallTracker } from './tool-call-tracker.js'
    10→import { DraftManager } from './draft-manager.js'
    11→import { ActivityTracker } from './activity.js'
    12→import { SkillCommandManager } from './skill-command-manager.js'
    13→import { PermissionHandler } from './permissions.js'
    14→import {
    15→  ensureForums,
    16→  createSessionThread as forumsCreateThread,
    17→  renameSessionThread as forumsRenameThread,
    18→  deleteSessionThread as forumsDeleteThread,
    19→  ensureUnarchived,
    20→  buildDeepLink,
    21→} from './forums.js'
    22→import {
    23→  registerSlashCommands,
    24→  handleSlashCommand,
    25→  setupButtonCallbacks,
    26→} from './commands/index.js'
    27→import {
    28→  spawnAssistant,
    29→  buildWelcomeMessage,
    30→} from './assistant.js'
    31→import type { Attachment } from '../../core/types.js'
    32→import type { FileService } from '../../core/file-service.js'
    33→import { buildFallbackText, downloadDiscordAttachment, isAttachmentTooLarge } from './media.js'
    34→
    35→export class DiscordAdapter extends ChannelAdapter<OpenACPCore> {
    36→  private client: Client
    37→  private discordConfig: DiscordChannelConfig
    38→  private sendQueue: DiscordSendQueue
    39→  private toolTracker: ToolCallTracker
    40→  private draftManager: DraftManager
    41→  private skillManager!: SkillCommandManager
    42→  private permissionHandler!: PermissionHandler
    43→  private sessionTrackers: Map<string, ActivityTracker> = new Map()
    44→  private guild!: Guild
    45→  private forumChannel!: ForumChannel | TextChannel
    46→  private notificationChannel!: TextChannel
    47→  private assistantSession: Session | null = null
    48→  private assistantInitializing = false
    49→  private fileService: FileService
    50→
    51→  constructor(core: OpenACPCore, config: DiscordChannelConfig) {
    52→    super(core, config)
    53→    this.discordConfig = config
    54→
    55→    this.client = new Client({
    56→      intents: [
    57→        GatewayIntentBits.Guilds,
    58→        GatewayIntentBits.GuildMessages,
    59→        GatewayIntentBits.MessageContent,
    60→      ],
    61→    })
    62→
    63→    this.sendQueue = new DiscordSendQueue()
    64→    this.toolTracker = new ToolCallTracker(this.sendQueue)
    65→    this.draftManager = new DraftManager(this.sendQueue)
    66→    this.fileService = core.fileService
    67→
    68→    // Wire discord.js rate limit events to send queue
    69→    this.client.rest.on('rateLimited', (info) => {
    70→      log.warn({ route: info.route, timeToReset: info.timeToReset }, '[DiscordAdapter] Rate limited')
    71→      this.sendQueue.onRateLimited()
    72→    })
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  // ─── start ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    76→
    77→  start(): Promise<void> {
    78→    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    79→      this.client.once('ready', async () => {
    80→        try {
    81→          log.info({ guildId: this.discordConfig.guildId }, '[DiscordAdapter] Client ready, initializing...')
    82→
    83→          // Fetch guild
    84→          const guild = this.client.guilds.cache.get(this.discordConfig.guildId)
    85→            ?? await this.client.guilds.fetch(this.discordConfig.guildId).catch(() => null)
    86→          if (!guild) {
    87→            throw new Error(`Guild not found: ${this.discordConfig.guildId}`)
    88→          }
    89→          this.guild = guild
    90→
    91→          // Ensure forum + notification channels exist
    92→          const saveConfig = (updates: Record<string, unknown>) =>
    93→            this.core.configManager.save(updates as Parameters<typeof this.core.configManager.save>[0])
    94→          const { forumChannel, notificationChannel } = await ensureForums(
    95→            guild,
    96→            {
    97→              forumChannelId: this.discordConfig.forumChannelId,
    98→              notificationChannelId: this.discordConfig.notificationChannelId,
    99→            },
   100→            saveConfig,
   101→          )
   102→          this.forumChannel = forumChannel
   103→          this.notificationChannel = notificationChannel
   104→
   105→          // Init managers that need guild/guildId
   106→          this.skillManager = new SkillCommandManager(this.sendQueue, this.core.sessionManager)
   107→          this.permissionHandler = new PermissionHandler(
   108→            guild.id,
   109→            (sessionId) => this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId),
   110→            (notification) => this.sendNotification(notification),
   111→          )
   112→
   113→          // Register slash commands
   114→          await registerSlashCommands(guild)
   115→
   116→          // Wire interaction + message handlers
   117→          this.setupInteractionHandler()
   118→          this.setupMessageHandler()
   119→
   120→          // Welcome message
   121→          const welcomeMsg = buildWelcomeMessage(this.core)
   122→          try {
   123→            await this.notificationChannel.send(welcomeMsg)
   124→          } catch (err) {
   125→            log.warn({ err }, '[DiscordAdapter] Failed to send welcome message')
   126→          }
   127→
   128→          // Spawn assistant session
   129→          await this.setupAssistant()
   130→
   131→          log.info('[DiscordAdapter] Initialization complete')
   132→          resolve()
   133→        } catch (err) {
   134→          log.error({ err }, '[DiscordAdapter] Initialization failed')
   135→          reject(err)
   136→        }
   137→      })
   138→
   139→      this.client.login(this.discordConfig.botToken).catch(reject)
   140→    })
   141→  }
   142→
   143→  // ─── stop ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   144→
   145→  async stop(): Promise<void> {
   146→    if (this.assistantSession) {
   147→      try {
   148→        await this.assistantSession.destroy()
   149→      } catch (err) {
   150→        log.warn({ err }, '[DiscordAdapter] Failed to destroy assistant session')
   151→      }
   152→      this.assistantSession = null
   153→    }
   154→    this.client.destroy()
   155→    log.info('[DiscordAdapter] Stopped')
   156→  }
   157→
   158→  // ─── Interaction handler ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   159→
   160→  private setupInteractionHandler(): void {
   161→    this.client.on('interactionCreate', async (interaction) => {
   162→      try {
   163→        if (interaction.isChatInputCommand()) {
   164→          await handleSlashCommand(interaction, this)
   165→          return
   166→        }
   167→
   168→        if (interaction.isButton()) {
   169→          // Permission buttons take priority
   170→          const handled = await this.permissionHandler.handleButtonInteraction(interaction)
   171→          if (!handled) {
   172→            await setupButtonCallbacks(interaction, this)
   173→          }
   174→        }
   175→      } catch (err) {
   176→        log.error({ err }, '[DiscordAdapter] interactionCreate handler error')
   177→      }
   178→    })
   179→  }
   180→
   181→  // ─── Message handler ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   182→
   183→  private setupMessageHandler(): void {
   184→    this.client.on('messageCreate', async (message) => {
   185→      try {
   186→        // Ignore bots and self
   187→        if (message.author.bot) return
   188→
   189→        // Ignore DMs
   190→        if (!message.guild) return
   191→
   192→        // Ignore messages from the wrong guild
   193→        if (message.guild.id !== this.guild.id) return
   194→
   195→        // Only process messages in threads
   196→        if (!message.channel.isThread()) return
   197→
   198→        const threadId = message.channel.id
   199→        const userId = message.author.id
   200→        let text = message.content
   201→
   202→        log.debug(
   203→          { threadId, userId, text: text.slice(0, 50), attachmentCount: message.attachments.size },
   204→          '[DiscordAdapter] messageCreate received',
   205→        )
   206→
   207→        // Ignore messages with no text and no attachments
   208→        if (!text && message.attachments.size === 0) return
   209→
   210→        // Resolve sessionId for file storage (fallback to "unknown" for new sessions)
   211→        const sessionId =
   212→          this.core.sessionManager.getSessionByThread('discord', threadId)?.id ?? 'unknown'
   213→
   214→        // Process attachments
   215→        if (message.attachments.size > 0) {
   216→          log.info(
   217→            {
   218→              sessionId,
   219→              attachments: message.attachments.map((a) => ({
   220→                name: a.name, size: a.size, contentType: a.contentType, url: a.url?.slice(0, 80),
   221→              })),
   222→            },
   223→            '[discord-media] Processing incoming attachments',
   224→          )
   225→        }
   226→        const attachments = await this.processIncomingAttachments(message, sessionId)
   227→
   228→        // Generate fallback text if message has attachments but no text
   229→        if (!text && attachments.length > 0) {
   230→          text = buildFallbackText(attachments)
   231→        }
   232→
   233→        // If all attachment downloads failed and no text, notify user
   234→        if (!text && attachments.length === 0 && message.attachments.size > 0) {
   235→          try {
   236→            await message.reply('Failed to process attachment(s)')
   237→          } catch { /* best effort */ }
   238→          return
   239→        }
   240→
   241→        // Route assistant thread messages to assistant
   242→        if (
   243→          this.discordConfig.assistantThreadId &&
   244→          threadId === this.discordConfig.assistantThreadId
   245→        ) {
   246→          if (this.assistantSession && text) {
   247→            await this.assistantSession.enqueuePrompt(text, attachments.length > 0 ? attachments : undefined)
   248→          }
   249→          return
   250→        }
   251→
   252→        // Route to core for session dispatch
   253→        await this.core.handleMessage({
   254→          channelId: 'discord',
   255→          threadId,
   256→          userId,
   257→          text,
   258→          ...(attachments.length > 0 ? { attachments } : {}),
   259→        })
   260→      } catch (err) {
   261→        log.error({ err }, '[DiscordAdapter] messageCreate handler error')
   262→      }
   263→    })
   264→  }
   265→
   266→  // ─── Assistant ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   267→
   268→  private async setupAssistant(): Promise<void> {
   269→    let threadId = this.discordConfig.assistantThreadId
   270→
   271→    // Verify existing thread is still accessible
   272→    if (threadId) {
   273→      try {
   274→        const existing = this.guild.channels.cache.get(threadId)
   275→          ?? await this.guild.channels.fetch(threadId)
   276→        if (existing && existing.isThread()) {
   277→          await ensureUnarchived(existing as import('discord.js').ThreadChannel)
   278→          log.info({ threadId }, '[DiscordAdapter] Reusing existing assistant thread')
   279→        } else {
   280→          log.warn({ threadId }, '[DiscordAdapter] Assistant thread not found, recreating...')
   281→          threadId = null
   282→        }
   283→      } catch {
   284→        log.warn({ threadId }, '[DiscordAdapter] Assistant thread inaccessible, recreating...')
   285→        threadId = null
   286→      }
   287→    }
   288→
   289→    if (!threadId) {
   290→      // Create a new thread for the assistant
   291→      const thread = await forumsCreateThread(this.forumChannel, 'Assistant')
   292→      threadId = thread.id
   293→      await this.core.configManager.save({
   294→        channels: { discord: { assistantThreadId: thread.id } },
   295→      } as Parameters<typeof this.core.configManager.save>[0])
   296→      log.info({ threadId }, '[DiscordAdapter] Created assistant thread')
   297→    }
   298→
   299→    this.assistantInitializing = true
   300→    try {
   301→      const { session, ready } = await spawnAssistant(this.core, threadId)
   302→      this.assistantSession = session
   303→      ready.finally(() => {
   304→        this.assistantInitializing = false
   305→      })
   306→    } catch (err) {
   307→      this.assistantInitializing = false
   308→      log.error({ err }, '[DiscordAdapter] Failed to spawn assistant')
   309→    }
   310→  }
   311→
   312→  async respawnAssistant(): Promise<void> {
   313→    if (this.assistantSession) {
   314→      try {
   315→        await this.assistantSession.destroy()
   316→      } catch { /* ignore */ }
   317→      this.assistantSession = null
   318→    }
   319→    await this.setupAssistant()
   320→  }
   321→
   322→  // ─── Incoming media ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   323→
   324→  private async processIncomingAttachments(
   325→    message: import('discord.js').Message,
   326→    sessionId: string,
   327→  ): Promise<Attachment[]> {
   328→    if (message.attachments.size === 0) return []
   329→
   330→    const isVoiceMessage = message.flags.has(MessageFlags.IsVoiceMessage)
   331→
   332→    const results = await Promise.allSettled(
   333→      message.attachments.map(async (discordAtt) => {
   334→        const buffer = await downloadDiscordAttachment(
   335→          discordAtt.url,
   336→          discordAtt.name ?? 'attachment',
   337→        )
   338→        if (!buffer) return null
   339→
   340→        let data = buffer
   341→        let fileName = discordAtt.name ?? 'attachment'
   342→        let mimeType = discordAtt.contentType ?? 'application/octet-stream'
   343→
   344→        // Convert voice messages from OGG Opus to WAV
   345→        if (isVoiceMessage && mimeType.includes('ogg')) {
   346→          try {
   347→            data = await this.fileService.convertOggToWav(buffer)
   348→            fileName = 'voice.wav'
   349→            mimeType = 'audio/wav'
   350→          } catch (err) {
   351→            log.warn({ err }, '[discord-media] OGG→WAV conversion failed, saving original')
   352→          }
   353→        }
   354→
   355→        return this.fileService.saveFile(sessionId, fileName, data, mimeType)
   356→      }),
   357→    )
   358→
   359→    const rejected = results.filter((r) => r.status === 'rejected')
   360→    if (rejected.length > 0) {
   361→      log.warn({ rejected: rejected.map((r) => (r as PromiseRejectedResult).reason) }, '[discord-media] Some attachments failed')
   362→    }
   363→
   364→    const saved = results
   365→      .filter((r): r is PromiseFulfilledResult<Attachment | null> => r.status === 'fulfilled')
   366→      .map((r) => r.value)
   367→      .filter((att): att is Attachment => att !== null)
   368→
   369→    log.info({ count: saved.length, files: saved.map((a) => a.fileName) }, '[discord-media] Attachments processed')
   370→    return saved
   371→  }
   372→
   373→  // ─── Helper: resolve thread ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   374→
   375→  private async getThread(sessionId: string): Promise<ThreadChannel | null> {
   376→    const session = this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   377→    const threadId = session?.threadId
   378→    if (!threadId) {
   379→      log.warn({ sessionId }, '[DiscordAdapter] No threadId for session')
   380→      return null
   381→    }
   382→    try {
   383→      const channel = this.guild.channels.cache.get(threadId)
   384→        ?? await this.guild.channels.fetch(threadId)
   385→      if (channel && channel.isThread()) return channel as ThreadChannel
   386→      log.warn({ sessionId, threadId }, '[DiscordAdapter] Channel is not a thread')
   387→      return null
   388→    } catch (err) {
   389→      log.warn({ err, sessionId, threadId }, '[DiscordAdapter] Failed to fetch thread')
   390→      return null
   391→    }
   392→  }
   393→
   394→  // ─── sendMessage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   395→
   396→  async sendMessage(sessionId: string, content: OutgoingMessage): Promise<void> {
   397→    // Suppress output while assistant is initializing its system prompt
   398→    if (
   399→      this.assistantInitializing &&
   400→      this.assistantSession &&
   401→      sessionId === this.assistantSession.id
   402→    ) {
   403→      return
   404→    }
   405→
   406→    const thread = await this.getThread(sessionId)
   407→    if (!thread) return
   408→
   409→    await ensureUnarchived(thread)
   410→
   411→    const isAssistant =
   412→      this.assistantSession != null && sessionId === this.assistantSession.id
   413→
   414→    // Get or create activity tracker for this session
   415→    if (!this.sessionTrackers.has(sessionId)) {
   416→      this.sessionTrackers.set(sessionId, new ActivityTracker(thread, this.sendQueue))
   417→    }
   418→    const tracker = this.sessionTrackers.get(sessionId)!
   419→
   420→    switch (content.type) {
   421→      case 'thought': {
   422→        await tracker.onThought()
   423→        break
   424→      }
   425→
   426→      case 'text': {
   427→        await tracker.onTextStart()
   428→        const draft = this.draftManager.getOrCreate(sessionId, thread)
   429→        draft.append(content.text)
   430→        this.draftManager.appendText(sessionId, content.text)
   431→        break
   432→      }
   433→
   434→      case 'tool_call': {
   435→        await tracker.onToolCall()
   436→        await this.draftManager.finalize(sessionId, thread, isAssistant)
   437→        const meta = content.metadata ?? {}
   438→        await this.toolTracker.trackNewCall(sessionId, thread, {
   439→          id: String(meta.id ?? ''),
   440→          name: content.text || String(meta.name ?? 'Tool'),
   441→          kind: meta.kind as string | undefined,
   442→          status: String(meta.status ?? 'running'),
   443→          content: meta.content,
   444→          viewerLinks: meta.viewerLinks as { file?: string; diff?: string } | undefined,
   445→          viewerFilePath: meta.viewerFilePath as string | undefined,
   446→        })
   447→        break
   448→      }
   449→
   450→      case 'tool_update': {
   451→        const meta = content.metadata ?? {}
   452→        await this.toolTracker.updateCall(sessionId, {
   453→          id: String(meta.id ?? ''),
   454→          name: content.text || String(meta.name ?? ''),
   455→          kind: meta.kind as string | undefined,
   456→          status: String(meta.status ?? 'completed'),
   457→          content: meta.content,
   458→          viewerLinks: meta.viewerLinks as { file?: string; diff?: string } | undefined,
   459→          viewerFilePath: meta.viewerFilePath as string | undefined,
   460→        })
   461→        break
   462→      }
   463→
   464→      case 'plan': {
   465→        const entries = (content.metadata?.entries ?? []) as PlanEntry[]
   466→        await tracker.onPlan(entries)
   467→        break
   468→      }
   469→
   470→      case 'usage': {
   471→        await this.draftManager.finalize(sessionId, thread, isAssistant)
   472→        const meta = content.metadata ?? {}
   473→        await tracker.sendUsage({
   474→          tokensUsed: meta.tokensUsed as number | undefined,
   475→          contextSize: meta.contextSize as number | undefined,
   476→        })
   477→        // Send usage notification to notification channel
   478→        try {
   479→          const deepLink = buildDeepLink(this.guild.id, thread.id)
   480→          await this.sendNotification({
   481→            sessionId,
   482→            type: 'completed',
   483→            summary: content.text || 'Session completed',
   484→            deepLink,
   485→          })
   486→        } catch { /* best effort */ }
   487→        break
   488→      }
   489→
   490→      case 'session_end': {
   491→        await this.draftManager.finalize(sessionId, thread, isAssistant)
   492→        await tracker.cleanup()
   493→        this.toolTracker.cleanup(sessionId)
   494→        this.sessionTrackers.delete(sessionId)
   495→        await this.skillManager.cleanup(sessionId)
   496→        try {
   497→          await this.sendQueue.enqueue(
   498→            () => thread.send({ content: '✅ Done' }),
   499→            { type: 'other' },
   500→          )
   501→        } catch { /* best effort */ }
   502→        break
   503→      }
   504→
   505→      case 'error': {
   506→        await this.draftManager.finalize(sessionId, thread, isAssistant)
   507→        await tracker.cleanup()
   508→        this.toolTracker.cleanup(sessionId)
   509→        this.sessionTrackers.delete(sessionId)
   510→        try {
   511→          await this.sendQueue.enqueue(
   512→            () => thread.send({ content: `❌ Error: ${content.text}` }),
   513→            { type: 'other' },
   514→          )
   515→        } catch { /* best effort */ }
   516→        break
   517→      }
   518→
   519→      case 'attachment': {
   520→        if (!content.attachment) break
   521→        const { attachment } = content
   522→        await this.draftManager.finalize(sessionId, thread, isAssistant)
   523→
   524→        // Discord free tier limit: 25MB
   525→        if (isAttachmentTooLarge(attachment.size)) {
   526→          log.warn({ sessionId, fileName: attachment.fileName, size: attachment.size }, '[discord-media] File too large (>25MB)')
   527→          try {
   528→            await this.sendQueue.enqueue(
   529→              () => thread.send({ content: `⚠️ File too large to send (${Math.round(attachment.size / 1024 / 1024)}MB): ${attachment.fileName}` }),
   530→              { type: 'other' },
   531→            )
   532→          } catch { /* best effort */ }
   533→          break
   534→        }
   535→
   536→        try {
   537→          await this.sendQueue.enqueue(
   538→            () => thread.send({ files: [{ attachment: attachment.filePath, name: attachment.fileName }] }),
   539→            { type: 'other' },
   540→          )
   541→        } catch (err) {
   542→          log.error({ err, sessionId, fileName: attachment.fileName }, '[discord-media] Failed to send attachment')
   543→        }
   544→        break
   545→      }
   546→    }
   547→  }
   548→
   549→  // ─── sendPermissionRequest ────────────────────────────────────────────────
   550→
   551→  async sendPermissionRequest(sessionId: string, request: PermissionRequest): Promise<void> {
   552→    const session = this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   553→    if (!session) {
   554→      log.warn({ sessionId }, '[DiscordAdapter] sendPermissionRequest: session not found')
   555→      return
   556→    }
   557→
   558→    // Auto-approve if request is from openacp internals or dangerous mode is enabled
   559→    const autoApprove =
   560→      request.description.toLowerCase().includes('openacp') ||
   561→      session.dangerousMode
   562→
   563→    if (autoApprove) {
   564→      const allowOption = request.options.find((o) => o.isAllow)
   565→      if (allowOption && session.permissionGate.requestId === request.id) {
   566→        session.permissionGate.resolve(allowOption.id)
   567→      }
   568→      return
   569→    }
   570→
   571→    const thread = await this.getThread(sessionId)
   572→    if (!thread) return
   573→
   574→    await this.permissionHandler.sendPermissionRequest(session, request, thread)
   575→  }
   576→
   577→  // ─── sendNotification ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   578→
   579→  async sendNotification(notification: NotificationMessage): Promise<void> {
   580→    if (!this.notificationChannel) return
   581→
   582→    const typeIcon: Record<string, string> = {
   583→      completed: '✅',
   584→      error: '❌',
   585→      permission: '🔐',
   586→      input_required: '💬',
   587→    }
   588→
   589→    const icon = typeIcon[notification.type] ?? 'ℹ️'
   590→    const name = notification.sessionName ? ` **${notification.sessionName}**` : ''
   591→    let text = `${icon}${name}: ${notification.summary}`
   592→    if (notification.deepLink) {
   593→      text += `\n${notification.deepLink}`
   594→    }
   595→
   596→    try {
   597→      await this.sendQueue.enqueue(
   598→        () => this.notificationChannel.send({ content: text }),
   599→        { type: 'other' },
   600→      )
   601→    } catch (err) {
   602→      log.warn({ err }, '[DiscordAdapter] Failed to send notification')
   603→    }
   604→  }
   605→
   606→  // ─── createSessionThread ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   607→
   608→  async createSessionThread(sessionId: string, name: string): Promise<string> {
   609→    const thread = await forumsCreateThread(this.forumChannel, name)
   610→
   611→    // Persist threadId on session record
   612→    const session = this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   613→    if (session) {
   614→      session.threadId = thread.id
   615→    }
   616→
   617→    const record = this.core.sessionManager.getSessionRecord(sessionId)
   618→    if (record) {
   619→      await this.core.sessionManager.patchRecord(sessionId, {
   620→        platform: { ...record.platform, threadId: thread.id },
   621→      })
   622→    }
   623→
   624→    return thread.id
   625→  }
   626→
   627→  // ─── renameSessionThread ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   628→
   629→  async renameSessionThread(sessionId: string, newName: string): Promise<void> {
   630→    const session = this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   631→    const threadId = session?.threadId
   632→    if (!threadId) return
   633→    await forumsRenameThread(this.guild, threadId, newName)
   634→  }
   635→
   636→  // ─── deleteSessionThread ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   637→
   638→  override async deleteSessionThread(sessionId: string): Promise<void> {
   639→    const session = this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   640→    const threadId = session?.threadId
   641→    if (!threadId) return
   642→    await forumsDeleteThread(this.guild, threadId)
   643→  }
   644→
   645→  // ─── sendSkillCommands ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   646→
   647→  override async sendSkillCommands(sessionId: string, commands: AgentCommand[]): Promise<void> {
   648→    const thread = await this.getThread(sessionId)
   649→    if (!thread) return
   650→    await this.skillManager.send(sessionId, thread, commands)
   651→  }
   652→
   653→  // ─── cleanupSkillCommands ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   654→
   655→  override async cleanupSkillCommands(sessionId: string): Promise<void> {
   656→    await this.skillManager.cleanup(sessionId)
   657→  }
   658→
   659→  // ─── Public helpers (for slash commands) ─────────────────────────────────
   660→
   661→  getForumChannel(): ForumChannel | TextChannel {
   662→    return this.forumChannel
   663→  }
   664→
   665→  getGuild(): Guild {
   666→    return this.guild
   667→  }
   668→
   669→  getGuildId(): string {
   670→    return this.guild.id
   671→  }
   672→
   673→  getAssistantSessionId(): string | null {
   674→    return this.assistantSession?.id ?? null
   675→  }
   676→
   677→  getAssistantThreadId(): string | null {
   678→    return this.discordConfig.assistantThreadId
   679→  }
   680→}

1→# Getting Started
     2→
     3→## Prerequisites
     4→
     5→- Node.js >= 20
     6→- At least one ACP agent installed (e.g., `@zed-industries/claude-agent-acp`)
     7→- A messaging platform — Telegram, Discord, or both:
     8→  - **Telegram**: A bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) + a Supergroup with **Topics** enabled
     9→  - **Discord**: A bot from [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) + a server with Manage Channels permissions
    10→
    11→## Install
    12→
    13→```bash
    14→npm install -g @openacp/cli
    15→```
    16→
    17→## First Run
    18→
    19→```bash
    20→openacp
    21→```
    22→
    23→On first run (no config file), an **interactive setup wizard** guides you through:
    24→
    25→### Step 1: Choose Channel
    26→
    27→- Pick your messaging platform: **Telegram**, **Discord**, or **Both**
    28→
    29→### Step 2: Configure Channel(s)
    30→
    31→**Telegram** (if selected):
    32→- Enter your bot token from @BotFather
    33→- Token is **validated** against the Telegram API — you'll see the bot name on success
    34→- OpenACP **auto-detects** your supergroup by listening for messages (120s timeout)
    35→- Send any message in your group while it's listening, or enter the chat ID manually
    36→- Validates that it's a supergroup (required for forum topics)
    37→
    38→**Discord** (if selected):
    39→- Enter your bot token from the Discord Developer Portal
    40→- Token is validated against the Discord API
    41→- Select your server from detected guilds
    42→
    43→### Step 3: Agents & Workspace
    44→
    45→- The wizard automatically scans your system for known ACP agents (`claude-agent-acp`, `claude-code`, `claude`, `codex`)
    46→- The first detected agent becomes the default
    47→- Optionally install Claude CLI integration for session transfer (`/openacp:handoff`)
    48→- Choose a base directory for project workspaces (default: `~/openacp-workspace`)
    49→
    50→### Step 4: Run Mode
    51→
    52→- Choose **foreground** (logs in terminal) or **daemon** (background service with auto-start)
    53→
    54→### Done
    55→
    56→Config is saved to `~/.openacp/config.json`. Edit it anytime — see [Configuration](configuration.md).
    57→
    58→## What Happens on Startup
    59→
    60→1. Config loaded and validated (Zod schema)
    61→2. Logger initialized (Pino with file rotation)
    62→3. Session store loaded (`~/.openacp/sessions.json`)
    63→4. Tunnel service started (if enabled — default: Cloudflare)
    64→5. Channel adapters registered and started
    65→6. System topics created in Telegram (Notifications + Assistant)
    66→7. Ready for messages
    67→
    68→## Running as a Daemon
    69→
    70→After setup, you can run OpenACP as a background service:
    71→
    72→```bash
    73→openacp start          # Start daemon
    74→openacp stop           # Stop daemon
    75→openacp status         # Check status
    76→openacp logs           # View logs
    77→```
    78→
    79→Or configure daemon mode as default via `openacp config` → Run Mode.
    80→
    81→## Next Steps
    82→
    83→- [Telegram Setup](telegram-setup.md) — detailed bot & group configuration
    84→- [Usage Guide](usage.md) — CLI commands, API, sessions, workspaces
    85→- [Configuration Reference](configuration.md) — all config options including API and run mode
    86→- [Tunnel & File Viewer](tunnel.md) — shareable code viewer
    87→

1→# OpenACP Setup Guide
     2→
     3→## Prerequisites
     4→
     5→Before starting, make sure you have:
     6→
     7→- **Node.js >= 20** installed
     8→- A **Telegram bot token** — create one via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)
     9→- A **Telegram Supergroup** with **Topics/Forum** enabled
    10→- At least one ACP agent installed (e.g., `claude-agent-acp`)
    11→
    12→## Install
    13→
    14→```bash
    15→npm install -g @openacp/cli
    16→```
    17→
    18→Or from source:
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→git clone https://github.com/nicepkg/OpenACP.git
    22→cd OpenACP
    23→pnpm install
    24→pnpm build
    25→```
    26→
    27→## First Run — Interactive Setup
    28→
    29→```bash
    30→openacp
    31→```
    32→
    33→If no config file exists (`~/.openacp/config.json`), the interactive setup wizard starts automatically. After setup, OpenACP starts immediately.
    34→
    35→### Step 1: Telegram
    36→
    37→The wizard asks for:
    38→
    39→1. **Bot token** — paste the token from BotFather. OpenACP validates it by calling the Telegram API (`getMe`). If validation fails, you can re-enter or skip.
    40→2. **Chat ID** — the numeric ID of your supergroup (e.g. `-1001234567890`). OpenACP validates it via `getChat` and checks that Topics are enabled.
    41→
    42→**How to get your Chat ID:**
    43→- Add [@raw_data_bot](https://t.me/raw_data_bot) to your group
    44→- Send a message in the group
    45→- The bot replies with the chat info including the ID
    46→
    47→**How to set up your Telegram group:**
    48→1. Create a new group in Telegram
    49→2. Convert to Supergroup (Settings → Group Type)
    50→3. Enable Topics (Settings → Topics → Enable)
    51→4. Add your bot as admin with **Manage Topics** permission
    52→
    53→### Step 2: Agents
    54→
    55→The wizard auto-detects installed agents in your PATH and `node_modules/.bin`:
    56→
    57→| Binary | Agent name |
    58→|--------|------------|
    59→| `claude-agent-acp` | claude |
    60→| `claude-code` / `claude` | claude |
    61→| `codex` | codex |
    62→
    63→Agents are auto-configured — `claude-agent-acp` is preferred when available.
    64→
    65→### Step 3: Workspace
    66→
    67→Choose the base directory where OpenACP creates project workspaces.
    68→
    69→Default: `~/openacp-workspace`
    70→
    71→When you create sessions with named workspaces (e.g. `/new claude my-app`), they go under this directory (`~/openacp-workspace/my-app/`).
    72→
    73→Config is saved automatically and OpenACP starts right away.
    74→
    75→## Config File
    76→
    77→Location: `~/.openacp/config.json` (override with `OPENACP_CONFIG_PATH` env var)
    78→
    79→```json
    80→{
    81→  "channels": {
    82→    "telegram": {
    83→      "enabled": true,
    84→      "botToken": "123456:ABC-DEF...",
    85→      "chatId": -1001234567890,
    86→      "notificationTopicId": null,
    87→      "assistantTopicId": null
    88→    }
    89→  },
    90→  "agents": {
    91→    "claude": {
    92→      "command": "claude-agent-acp",
    93→      "args": [],
    94→      "env": {}
    95→    }
    96→  },
    97→  "defaultAgent": "claude",
    98→  "workspace": {
    99→    "baseDir": "~/openacp-workspace"
   100→  },
   101→  "security": {
   102→    "allowedUserIds": [],
   103→    "maxConcurrentSessions": 5,
   104→    "sessionTimeoutMinutes": 60
   105→  }
   106→}
   107→```
   108→
   109→`notificationTopicId` and `assistantTopicId` are auto-created by OpenACP on first start — you don't need to set them.
   110→
   111→Security settings use defaults (all users allowed, 5 concurrent sessions, 60 min timeout). Edit the config file manually to change them.
   112→
   113→## Environment Variables
   114→
   115→These override config file values (useful for secrets or CI):
   116→
   117→| Variable | Overrides |
   118→|----------|-----------|
   119→| `OPENACP_CONFIG_PATH` | Config file location |
   120→| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | `channels.telegram.botToken` |
   121→| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` | `channels.telegram.chatId` |
   122→| `OPENACP_DEFAULT_AGENT` | `defaultAgent` |
   123→| `OPENACP_DEBUG` | Enable debug logging (`1`) |
   124→
   125→## Plugins
   126→
   127→Install additional adapters:
   128→
   129→```bash
   130→openacp install @openacp/adapter-discord
   131→openacp plugins                              # list installed
   132→openacp uninstall @openacp/adapter-discord   # remove
   133→```
   134→
   135→Configure in `~/.openacp/config.json`:
   136→
   137→```json
   138→{
   139→  "channels": {
   140→    "discord": {
   141→      "enabled": true,
   142→      "adapter": "@openacp/adapter-discord",
   143→      "botToken": "..."
   144→    }
   145→  }
   146→}
   147→```
   148→
   149→## Re-running Setup
   150→
   151→To re-run the setup wizard:
   152→
   153→```bash
   154→rm ~/.openacp/config.json
   155→openacp
   156→```
   157→
   158→## Using OpenACP
   159→
   160→Once running, OpenACP auto-creates two topics in your Telegram group:
   161→- **Notifications** — aggregated alerts with deep links
   162→- **Assistant** — AI helper for managing sessions
   163→
   164→### Commands
   165→
   166→| Command | Description |
   167→|---------|-------------|
   168→| `/new [agent] [workspace]` | Create a new session |
   169→| `/newchat` | New session, same agent & workspace |
   170→| `/cancel` | Cancel current session |
   171→| `/status` | Show session or system status |
   172→| `/agents` | List available agents |
   173→| `/help` | Show help |
   174→
   175→### Examples
   176→
   177→```
   178→/new claude my-app          → Claude session in ~/openacp-workspace/my-app/
   179→/new codex api-server       → Codex session in ~/openacp-workspace/api-server/
   180→/new claude ~/code/project  → Claude session with absolute path
   181→/new                        → Default agent and workspace
   182→```
   183→
   184→### Session Flow
   185→
   186→1. `/new claude my-project` — bot creates a new topic
   187→2. Send your coding request in the topic
   188→3. Agent responds with streaming text, tool calls, and code
   189→4. When agent needs permission (run command, edit file) — inline buttons appear
   190→5. Click Allow/Deny — agent continues
   191→6. `/cancel` to stop, or start a new topic with `/new`
   192→
   193→## Troubleshooting
   194→
   195→**"No channels enabled"** — Your config has `"enabled": false` for Telegram. Re-run setup or edit config manually.
   196→
   197→**Bot token validation fails** — Make sure the token from BotFather is correct and the bot hasn't been revoked.
   198→
   199→**Chat ID validation fails** — Ensure the chat is a Supergroup (not a regular group) and the bot is a member.
   200→
   201→**Topics not enabled** — Go to group settings → Topics → Enable. The group must be a Supergroup first.
   202→
   203→**Agent not found** — Install the agent binary and make sure it's in your PATH. Run `which claude-agent-acp` to verify.
   204→

1→# Discord Adapter Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
     4→
     5→**Goal:** Add a built-in Discord adapter with full feature parity with the Telegram adapter.
     6→
     7→**Architecture:** Mirror the Telegram adapter 1:1 in `src/adapters/discord/`, using discord.js. Each session maps to a Discord forum channel post. Slash commands replace text commands. Button components replace inline keyboards.
     8→
     9→**Tech Stack:** discord.js v14+, TypeScript ESM, Vitest
    10→
    11→**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-23-discord-adapter-design.md`
    12→
    13→**Critical API Notes (verified against actual codebase):**
    14→- `sessionManager.listSessions(channelId?)` — NOT `getAllSessions()`
    15→- `sessionManager.listRecords(filter?)` — for listing stored records
    16→- `sessionManager.getSession(id)` — returns `Session | undefined`
    17→- `sessionManager.getSessionByThread(channelId, threadId)` — in-memory lookup
    18→- `sessionManager.patchRecord(id, patch)` — update stored record
    19→- `sessionManager.cancelSession(id)` — abort + mark cancelled
    20→- `agentManager.getAvailableAgents()` — NOT `getInstalledAgents()`
    21→- `agentManager.getAgent(name)` — returns `AgentDefinition | undefined`
    22→- `core.handleNewSession(channelId, agentName?, workspacePath?)` — 3 positional args, NOT an object
    23→- `core.createSession(params)` — takes `{ channelId, agentName, workingDirectory, ... }`
    24→- `configManager.save(updates)` — uses **deep merge with nested objects**, NOT dot-path strings. E.g. `save({ channels: { discord: { forumChannelId: '123' } } })` NOT `save({ 'channels.discord.forumChannelId': '123' })`
    25→- `core.ts` line 236: `platform.topicId = Number(session.threadId)` — Telegram-specific, will lose precision for Discord snowflakes. **Task 13 must fix this to be channel-aware.**
    26→- `getRecordByThread()` uses `(p) => String(p.topicId) === threadId` — Telegram-specific. **Task 13 must fix for Discord.**
    27→
    28→---
    29→
    30→### Task 1: Foundation — Types, Config, Dependencies
    31→
    32→**Files:**
    33→- Create: `src/adapters/discord/types.ts`
    34→- Create: `src/adapters/discord/index.ts`
    35→- Modify: `src/core/types.ts:197-201` (add DiscordPlatformData)
    36→- Modify: `src/core/config.ts:247-267` (add env overrides)
    37→- Modify: `package.json` (add discord.js)
    38→
    39→- [ ] **Step 1: Install discord.js**
    40→
    41→```bash
    42→pnpm add discord.js
    43→```
    44→
    45→- [ ] **Step 2: Add DiscordPlatformData to core types**
    46→
    47→In `src/core/types.ts` after `TelegramPlatformData` (line 200), add:
    48→
    49→```ts
    50→export interface DiscordPlatformData {
    51→  threadId: string;
    52→  skillMsgId?: string;
    53→}
    54→```
    55→
    56→- [ ] **Step 3: Create `src/adapters/discord/types.ts`**
    57→
    58→```ts
    59→import type { Session } from '../../core/session.js'
    60→
    61→export interface DiscordChannelConfig {
    62→  enabled: boolean
    63→  botToken: string
    64→  guildId: string
    65→  forumChannelId: string | null
    66→  notificationChannelId: string | null
    67→  assistantThreadId: string | null
    68→}
    69→
    70→export interface CommandsAssistantContext {
    71→  threadId: string
    72→  getSession: () => Session | null
    73→  respawn: () => Promise<void>
    74→}
    75→```
    76→
    77→- [ ] **Step 4: Create `src/adapters/discord/index.ts`**
    78→
    79→```ts
    80→export { DiscordAdapter } from './adapter.js'
    81→export type { DiscordChannelConfig } from './types.js'
    82→```
    83→
    84→Note: `adapter.ts` doesn't exist yet — this will cause a TS error until Task 10. That's fine.
    85→
    86→- [ ] **Step 5: Add Discord env overrides to `config.ts`**
    87→
    88→In `src/core/config.ts` inside `applyEnvOverrides()`, add to the `overrides` array (after the Telegram entries):

    92→["OPENACP_DISCORD_GUILD_ID", ["channels", "discord", "guildId"]],
    93→```

## Summary: Discord Setup/Onboarding Flow in OpenACP

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's a complete analysis of how the Discord setup and onboarding flow works:

---

### **1. SETUP WIZARD FLOW (src/core/setup.ts)**

The Discord setup is part of an interactive wizard triggered on first run when no config file exists. The flow:

#### **Channel Selection** (Line 637-645)
- User chooses: **Telegram**, **Discord**, or **Both**
- Dynamic step counting based on selections

#### **Discord Setup Function** (Line 426-472)
The `setupDiscord()` function:

1. **Bot Token Prompt** (Lines 432-452)
   - Prompt: `"Bot token (from Discord Developer Portal):"`
   - Validates: Token cannot be empty
   - Calls `validateDiscordToken()` (Line 438)
   - On success: Shows bot username and ID
   - On failure: User can retry or skip validation

2. **Guild ID Prompt** (Lines 454-462)
   - Prompt: `"Guild (server) ID:"`
   - Validation: Must be 17-20 digit snowflake (Discord numeric ID format)
   - Regex: `/^\d{17,20}$/`

3. **Return Structure** (Lines 464-471)
   ```typescript
   {
     enabled: true,
     botToken: string,
     guildId: string,
     forumChannelId: null,        // Auto-created on adapter startup
     notificationChannelId: null, // Auto-created on adapter startup
     assistantThreadId: null      // Auto-created on adapter startup
   }
   ```

---

### **2. TOKEN VALIDATION (src/core/setup.ts, Lines 405-424)**

The `validateDiscordToken()` function:

```typescript
- Endpoint: https://discord.com/api/v10/users/@me
- Authorization header: "Bot {token}"
- Success (200): Returns { ok: true, username, id }
- Unauthorized (401): Returns { ok: false, error: "Token rejected by Discord (401 Unauthorized)" }
- Other errors: Returns { ok: false, error: `Discord API error {status}` }
```

---

### **3. CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT (src/core/config.ts)**

#### **Config Schema** (Lines 60-93)
- Uses Zod validation with `BaseChannelSchema` for all channels
- Supports `.passthrough()` for extra fields

#### **Discord Default Config** (Lines 113-120)
```json
{
  "discord": {
    "enabled": false,
    "botToken": "YOUR_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_HERE",
    "guildId": "",
    "forumChannelId": null,
    "notificationChannelId": null,
    "assistantThreadId": null
  }
}
```

#### **Environment Variable Overrides** (Lines 255-264)
- `OPENACP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` → `channels.discord.botToken`
- `OPENACP_DISCORD_GUILD_ID` → `channels.discord.guildId`

#### **Backward Compatibility**
- All fields use `.default()` or `.optional()` for safe migrations
- Config uses deep merge strategy for nested objects:
  ```typescript
  save({ channels: { discord: { forumChannelId: '123' } } })
  ```

---

### **4. DISCORD ADAPTER INITIALIZATION (src/adapters/discord/adapter.ts)**

#### **Startup Sequence** (Lines 77-141)
On `adapter.start()`:

1. **Discord.js Client Setup** (Lines 55-61)
   - Intents: `Guilds`, `GuildMessages`, `MessageContent`
   - Required: MESSAGE_CONTENT_INTENT (privileged intent)

2. **Guild Verification** (Lines 84-89)
   - Fetch guild by ID
   - Throws error if guild not found or inaccessible

3. **Forum/Notification Channel Setup** (Lines 94-101)
   - Calls `ensureForums()` from `forums.ts`
   - Creates channels if missing (IDs are null)
   - Persists IDs to config via deep merge

4. **Manager Initialization** (Lines 105-111)
   - Creates `SkillCommandManager`
   - Creates `PermissionHandler`

5. **Slash Command Registration** (Line 114)
   - Guild-scoped commands (faster propagation than global)
   - Full replace strategy: `guild.commands.set()` with all commands

6. **Event Handlers Setup** (Lines 117-118)
   - `interactionCreate` for slash commands and buttons
   - `messageCreate` for user messages in threads

7. **Welcome Message** (Lines 121-126)
   - Sent to notification channel
   - Best-effort delivery

8. **Assistant Session** (Line 129)
   - Spawns dedicated Discord assistant session
   - Runs in separate thread

#### **Shutdown** (Lines 145-156)
- Destroys assistant session
- Calls `client.destroy()` for graceful disconnect

---

### **5. FORUM CHANNEL MANAGEMENT (src/adapters/discord/forums.ts)**

#### **ensureForums()** (Lines 13-83)
- **Forum Channel Strategy**:
  - If guild has COMMUNITY feature: Creates forum channel (ChannelType.GuildForum)
  - Fallback: Creates text channel with threads (if not Community)
  - Reuses existing channel if ID is provided and accessible

- **Notification Channel**:
  - Always creates text channel
  - Named: `openacp-notifications`
  - Reuses existing if ID provided

- **Persistence**:
  - Saves channel IDs to config via nested object: `{ channels: { discord: { forumChannelId: ... } } }`

#### **createSessionThread()** (Lines 92-110)
- Forum Channel: Creates forum post (thread with initial message "⏳ Setting up...")
- Text Channel Fallback: Sends message, then creates thread on it

#### **ensureUnarchived()** (Lines 166-174)
- Auto-called before message sends
- Unarchives Discord threads (which auto-archive after inactivity)

#### **buildDeepLink()** (Lines 181-188)
- Builds Discord deep links: `https://discord.com/channels/{guildId}/{channelId}[/{messageId}]`

---

### **6. SLASH COMMANDS (src/adapters/discord/commands/index.ts)**

15 registered slash commands:
- `/new` - Create new session with optional agent + workspace
- `/newchat` - New chat in current thread
- `/cancel` - Cancel current session
- `/status` - Show status
- `/sessions` - List all sessions
- `/agents` - List available agents
- `/install` - Install agent by name
- `/menu` - Show action menu
- `/help` - Show help
- `/dangerous` - Toggle dangerous mode
- `/restart` - Restart OpenACP
- `/update` - Update to latest version
- `/integrate` - Manage integrations
- `/settings` - Show configuration
- `/doctor` - Run system diagnostics
- `/handoff` - Generate terminal resume command
- `/clear` - Reset assistant session

Registration uses guild-scoped full-replace: `guild.commands.set()`

---

### **7. DISCORD-SPECIFIC CONFIGURATION (src/adapters/discord/types.ts)**

```typescript
interface DiscordChannelConfig {
  enabled: boolean
  botToken: string
  guildId: string
  forumChannelId: string | null
  notificationChannelId: string | null
  assistantThreadId: string | null
  [key: string]: unknown  // passthrough for extensibility
}
```

---

### **8. ADAPTER REGISTRATION (src/main.ts, Lines 79-82)**

```typescript
if (channelName === 'discord') {
  const { DiscordAdapter } = await import('./adapters/discord/index.js')
  core.registerAdapter('discord', new DiscordAdapter(core, channelConfig as any))
  log.info({ adapter: 'discord' }, 'Adapter registered')
}
```

- Discord imported dynamically (not bundled)
- Only registered if `channels.discord.enabled === true`

---

### **9. DIAGNOSTIC CHECKS (src/core/doctor/checks/discord.ts)**

The `discordCheck` DoctorCheck runs 3 validations:

1. **Bot Token Format** (Lines 25-30)
   - Regex: `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,28}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,7}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{27,}$/`
   - Pattern: `<user_id>.<timestamp>.<hmac>` (base64-encoded)

2. **Token Validity** (Lines 32-53)
   - API call to `GET /users/@me` with Bot authorization
   - Confirms bot username and ID

3. **Guild Access** (Lines 55-82)
   - API call to `GET /guilds/{guildId}` with Bot authorization
   - Verifies bot is member of guild
   - Handles 403 (not member), 404 (guild not found)

---

### **10. DOCUMENTATION**

#### **Getting Started Guide** (`docs/guide/getting-started.md`)
- Lists Discord prerequisites: bot from Developer Portal + server with Manage Channels
- Step-by-step wizard flow for all channels

#### **Setup Spec** (`docs/specs/features/discord-adapter.md`)
- Defines forum channel + notification channel model
- Slash commands reference
- Config structure
- Error handling strategies

#### **Design Document** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-23-discord-adapter-design.md`)
- Comprehensive architecture (154+ lines)
- Platform mapping (Telegram ↔ Discord concepts)
- Startup sequence
- Event flow details
- Integration points
- Security & error handling

---

### **11. KEY FILES FOR DISCORD SETUP**

**Core Setup:**
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/core/setup.ts` — Interactive wizard (setupDiscord function at line 426)
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/core/config.ts` — Config schema + env overrides

**Discord Adapter:**
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/adapters/discord/adapter.ts` — Main adapter class (startup at line 77)
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/adapters/discord/types.ts` — DiscordChannelConfig interface
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/adapters/discord/forums.ts` — Forum/thread management
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/adapters/discord/commands/index.ts` — Slash command definitions

**Registration & Diagnostics:**
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/main.ts` — Adapter registration (line 79)
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/core/doctor/checks/discord.ts` — Diagnostic checks

**Documentation:**
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/docs/guide/getting-started.md`
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/docs/specs/features/discord-adapter.md`
- `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-23-discord-adapter-design.md`

---

### **12. PROMPTS AND USER FLOW**

When user runs `openacp` for first time:

```
Welcome to OpenACP

Which messaging platform do you want to use?
  ○ Telegram
  ○ Discord
  ◉ Both

[If Discord selected]
📱 Discord Setup

Bot token (from Discord Developer Portal): [INPUT - validated via API]
✓ Connected as @mybot (id: 123456789)

Guild (server) ID: [INPUT - must be 17-20 digits]

[Continues to agents, workspace, run mode...]

✓ Config saved to ~/.openacp/config.json
```

---

This comprehensive overview captures the complete Discord setup and onboarding flow from initial wizard prompts through adapter initialization, configuration management, and diagnostic verification.

- `OPENACP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` → `channels.discord.botToken`
- `OPENACP_DISCORD_GUILD_ID` → `channels.discord.guildId`

#### **Backward Compatibility**
- All fields use `.default()` or `.optional()` for safe migrations
- Config uses deep merge strategy for nested objects:
  ```typescript
  save({ channels: { discord: { forumChannelId: '123' } } })
  ```

---

### **4. DISCORD ADAPTER INITIALIZATION (src/adapters/discord/adapter.ts)**

#### **Startup Sequence** (Lines 77-141)
On `adapter.start()`:

1. **Discord.js Client Setup** (Lines 55-61)
   - Intents: `Guilds`, `GuildMessages`, `MessageContent`
   - Required: MESSAGE_CONTENT_INTENT (privileged intent)

2. **Guild Verification** (Lines 84-89)
   - Fetch guild by ID
   - Throws error if guild not found or inaccessible

3. **Forum/Notification Channel Setup** (Lines 94-101)
   - Calls `ensureForums()` from `forums.ts`
   - Creates channels if missing (IDs are null)
   - Persists IDs to config via deep merge

4. **Manager Initialization** (Lines 105-111)
   - Creates `SkillCommandManager`
   - Creates `PermissionHandler`

5. **Slash Command Registration** (Line 114)
   - Guild-scoped commands (faster propagation than global)
   - Full replace strategy: `guild.commands.set()` with all commands

6. **Event Handlers Setup** (Lines 117-118)
   - `interactionCreate` for slash commands and buttons
   - `messageCreate` for user messages in threads

7. **Welcome Message** (Lines 121-126)
   - Sent to notification channel
   - Best-effort delivery

8. **Assistant Session** (Line 129)
   - Spawns dedicated Discord assistant session
   - Runs in separate thread

#### **Shutdown** (Lines 145-156)
- Destroys assistant session
- Calls `client.destroy()` for graceful disconnect

---

### **5. FORUM CHANNEL MANAGEMENT (src/adapters/discord/forums.ts)**

#### **ensureForums()** (Lines 13-83)
- **Forum Channel Strategy**:
  - If guild has COMMUNITY feature: Creates forum channel (ChannelType.GuildForum)
  - Fallback: Creates text channel with threads (if not Community)
  - Reuses existing channel if ID is provided and accessible

- **Notification Channel**:
  - Always creates text channel
  - Named: `openacp-notifications`
  - Reuses existing if ID provided

- **Persistence**:
  - Saves channel IDs to config via nested object: `{ channels: { discord: { forumChannelId: ... } } }`

#### **createSessionThread()** (Lines 92-110)
- Forum Channel: Creates forum post (thread with initial message "⏳ Setting up...")
- Text Channel Fallback: Sends message, then creates thread on it

#### **ensureUnarchived()** (Lines 166-174)
- Auto-called before message sends
- Unarchives Discord threads (which auto-archive after inactivity)

#### **buildDeepLink()** (Lines 181-188)
- Builds Discord deep links: `https://discord.com/channels/{guildId}/{channelId}[/{messageId}]`

---

### **6. SLASH COMMANDS (src/adapters/discord/commands/index.ts)**

15 registered slash commands:
- `/new` - Create new session with optional agent + workspace
- `/newchat` - New chat in current thread
- `/cancel` - Cancel current session
- `/status` - Show status
- `/sessions` - List all sessions
- `/agents` - List available agents
- `/install` - Install agent by name
- `/menu` - Show action menu
- `/help` - Show help
- `/dangerous` - Toggle dangerous mode
- `/restart` - Restart OpenACP
- `/update` - Update to latest version
- `/integrate` - Manage integrations
- `/settings` - Show configuration
- `/doctor` - Run system diagnostics
- `/handoff` - Generate terminal resume command
- `/clear` - Reset assistant session

Registration uses guild-scoped full-replace: `guild.commands.set()`

---

### **7. DISCORD-SPECIFIC CONFIGURATION (src/adapters/discord/types.ts)**

```typescript
interface DiscordChannelConfig {
  enabled: boolean
  botToken: string
  guildId: string
  forumChannelId: string | null
  notificationChannelId: string | null
  assistantThreadId: string | null
  [key: string]: unknown  // passthrough for extensibility
}
```

```typescript
if (channelName === 'discord') {
  const { DiscordAdapter } = await import('./adapters/discord/index.js')
  core.registerAdapter('discord', new DiscordAdapter(core, channelConfig as any))

# Getting Started

## Prerequisites

- Node.js >= 20
- At least one ACP agent installed (e.g., `@zed-industries/claude-agent-acp`)
- A messaging platform — Telegram, Discord, or both:
  - **Telegram**: A bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) + a Supergroup with **Topics** enabled
  - **Discord**: A bot from [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) + a server with Manage Channels permissions

## Install

```bash
npm install -g @openacp/cli
```

## First Run

```bash
openacp
```

On first run (no config file), an **interactive setup wizard** guides you through:

### Step 1: Choose Channel

- Pick your messaging platform: **Telegram**, **Discord**, or **Both**

### Step 2: Configure Channel(s)

**Telegram** (if selected):
- Enter your bot token from @BotFather
- Token is **validated** against the Telegram API — you'll see the bot name on success
- OpenACP **auto-detects** your supergroup by listening for messages (120s timeout)
- Send any message in your group while it's listening, or enter the chat ID manually
- Validates that it's a supergroup (required for forum topics)

**Discord** (if selected):
- Enter your bot token from the Discord Developer Portal
- Token is validated against the Discord API
- Select your server from detected guilds

### Step 3: Agents & Workspace

- The wizard automatically scans your system for known ACP agents (`claude-agent-acp`, `claude-code`, `claude`, `codex`)
- The first detected agent becomes the default
- Optionally install Claude CLI integration for session transfer (`/openacp:handoff`)
- Choose a base directory for project workspaces (default: `~/openacp-workspace`)

### Step 4: Run Mode

- Choose **foreground** (logs in terminal) or **daemon** (background service with auto-start)

### Done

Config is saved to `~/.openacp/config.json`. Edit it anytime — see [Configuration](configuration.md).

## What Happens on Startup

1. Config loaded and validated (Zod schema)
2. Logger initialized (Pino with file rotation)
3. Session store loaded (`~/.openacp/sessions.json`)
4. Tunnel service started (if enabled — default: Cloudflare)
5. Channel adapters registered and started
6. System topics created in Telegram (Notifications + Assistant)
7. Ready for messages

## Running as a Daemon

After setup, you can run OpenACP as a background service:

```bash
openacp start          # Start daemon
openacp stop           # Stop daemon
openacp status         # Check status
openacp logs           # View logs
```

Or configure daemon mode as default via `openacp config` → Run Mode.

## Next Steps

- [Telegram Setup](telegram-setup.md) — detailed bot & group configuration
- [Usage Guide](usage.md) — CLI commands, API, sessions, workspaces
- [Configuration Reference](configuration.md) — all config options including API and run mode
- [Tunnel & File Viewer](tunnel.md) — shareable code viewer

# Telegram Setup

## Create a Bot

1. Open [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) in Telegram
2. Send `/newbot`, follow the prompts
3. Copy the bot token

## Create a Supergroup

1. Create a new Group in Telegram
2. Go to **Group Settings** → enable **Topics**
3. This converts it to a Supergroup with forum topics

## Add Bot as Admin

Add your bot to the group and promote to **Admin** with:
- **Manage Topics** (required)
- **Send Messages**
- **Delete Messages** (optional)

## Get Chat ID

Forward any message from the group to [@RawDataBot](https://t.me/raw_data_bot). It replies with the chat ID (negative number starting with `-100`).

Or use the API directly:
```
https://api.telegram.org/bot<YOUR_TOKEN>/getUpdates
```

## System Topics

On first start, OpenACP creates two topics automatically:

| Topic | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| **Notifications** | Session completed, errors, permission requests — with deep links |
| **Assistant** | AI-powered helper that guides you through creating and managing sessions |

Topic IDs are saved to config (`notificationTopicId`, `assistantTopicId`).

## Session Topics

Each `/new` command creates a **separate forum topic** for that session. Features:

- **Real-time streaming** — agent responses stream as they're generated, with throttled message updates (1s interval)
- **Auto-naming** — after the first prompt, the topic is renamed to a 5-word summary
- **Prompt queue** — send multiple messages while agent is busy, they queue up
- **Skill commands** — agent publishes available skills as inline buttons, pinned in the topic
- **Permission buttons** — when agent needs approval, inline buttons appear (Allow / Always Allow / Reject)
- **Viewer links** — if tunnel is enabled, tool calls include clickable file/diff viewer links

## Message Streaming

Agent output is streamed in real-time using a `MessageDraft` system:
- Text buffers and flushes at 1-second intervals
- First chunk creates a new message, subsequent chunks edit it
- Markdown → Telegram HTML conversion with syntax highlighting
- Messages split at 4096 chars (Telegram limit)
- Graceful fallback to plain text if HTML parsing fails

## Environment Variables

```bash
OPENACP_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=your_token openacp
REDACTED openacp
```
